title: Indie Brief, Monday 26 October
description:
Good morning, this is Indie Brief for Monday 26 October.

Modern Times Review reports that the CME Social Impact Center has backed Michał Marczak's documentary Closure ahead of its 9 November release. The Sundance-premiered film will be paired with a regional campaign focused on loneliness among young people, marking the first acquisition by CME's new impact arm.

description:

description:

description:
Good morning, this is Indie Brief for Wednesday 21 October.

Deadline reports on documentary momentum heading into awards season. Four Oscar-contending features are gaining traction with critics and industry arbiters: American Doctor, To Hold a Mountain, Closure, and Once Upon a Time in Harlem. title: Indie Brief, Tuesday 20 October
description:
Good morning, this is Indie Brief for Tuesday 20 October.

Screen Daily reports that Mia Bays, director of the BFI Filmmaking Fund, is coming to the end of her five-year tenure. Bays has corrected the record about her role, noting that people often thought she ran the London Film Festival, the archive, and BFI Southbank as well. She's feeling energised as she prepares to move on from the position.

title: Indie Brief, Monday 19 October
description:
Good morning, this is Indie Brief for Monday 19 October.

Deadline reports that Yeon Sang-ho's psychological thriller Paradise Lost has sold to 118 territories worldwide. The Train to Busan director's film has secured deals including Twin for Japan, The Jokers Films for France, and Well Go USA for North America. description:

title: Indie Brief, Saturday 17 October
description:
Good morning, this is Indie Brief for Saturday 17 October.

Screen Daily reports that European film and TV organisations have issued a joint statement criticising a proposed cut to the AgoraEU cultural fund. The funding would be reduced from eight point six billion euros to six billion euros, which organisations say would be devastating for the screen sector across Europe.

title: Indie Brief, Friday 16 October
description:
Good morning, this is Indie Brief for Friday 16 October.

Screen Daily reports that Tessa Ross has said even successful producers are struggling to raise funding. Speaking to an audience in Rome, she noted that having made a film that worked doesn't guarantee anyone will trust you to make another one. It's a sobering reminder of the current state of independent film financing.
